events.speaker: OTTILIE
events.text: Half of that crate is cracked and the rest is crazed where you can't see it yet. Cheap glass throws a flame crooked and then dies in a wind, which is exactly the hour you wanted it. Let me at it before anybody else puts a hand in.

events.speaker: OTTILIE
events.text: Enough saved to do something with. A piece I've reheated and drawn myself holds a flame straighter than anything that comes packed in straw from Saint Louis, and I'll say so to whoever likes.

events.speaker: OTTILIE
events.text: You paid for a mend instead of buying new. Nobody in this county does that. I'll want a bench, a roof over the bench, and coal that isn't green.

events.speaker: OTTILIE
events.text: I know what a flame means to do at every heat there is. That's most of why I love the trade. You I can't predict at all, and I've quit wishing I could.
